questions.prompt: How should you give a slide a title that a screen reader will actually announce?
answerPool: Use a slide layout's Title placeholder
Type it into a plain text box and make the font bold and larger
Add it as a caption underneath the slide
Put it in the Notes section only

questions.prompt: What actually controls the order a screen reader announces the objects on a slide?
answerPool: Their left-to-right, top-to-bottom position on the canvas
The order they were originally pasted in, permanently
Alphabetical order of each object's name

questions.prompt: A slide uses red text for "over budget" and green text for "on budget", with no other difference. What's the accessibility problem?
answerPool: Color alone is conveying the meaning, with no second cue for anyone who can't distinguish the colors
Nothing - red and green are commonly understood colors
Red and green text is never allowed in a slide deck
The font size is too small
